title: Rolling Changes Across a Fleet: serial and Failure Limits
intro: By default Ansible runs each task on every host in parallel, which is great for speed and catastrophic for a change that needs a restart. Rolling updates change a few hosts at a time and stop automatically when too many fail. The playbook patch.yml here uses 'serial' and 'max_fail_percentage'.

steps.prompt: Look at the play header in patch.yml, which controls batching.
steps.fake_output:
- name: Patch web servers
  hosts: web
  become: true
  serial: "25%"
  max_fail_percentage: 0
  pre_tasks:
    - name: Take host out of the load balancer
      ansible.builtin.command: /usr/local/bin/lb-drain {{ inventory_hostname }}
  tasks:
    - ansible.builtin.apt: {upgrade: dist, update_cache: true}
    - ansible.builtin.reboot: {reboot_timeout: 600}
steps.explanation: 25% of hosts per batch, and stop the whole run if any host in a batch fails.
steps.why: serial turns one big parallel run into sequential batches; the whole play (drain, patch, reboot, verify) completes on each batch before the next starts. max_fail_percentage: 0 means one failure stops everything, so a bad patch hits 25% of the fleet at most, never 100%.

steps.prompt: Run patch.yml against the 8 web hosts in inventory.ini.
steps.fake_output:
PLAY [Patch web servers] ***** (batch 1/4: web-01, web-02)
...
TASK [ansible.builtin.reboot] ***
changed: [web-01]
changed: [web-02]
TASK [Verify health endpoint] ***
ok: [web-01]
ok: [web-02]
PLAY [Patch web servers] ***** (batch 2/4: web-03, web-04)
...
TASK [Verify health endpoint] ***
fatal: [web-04]: FAILED! => {"status": 502}

NO MORE HOSTS LEFT *****
PLAY RECAP ***
web-01 : ok=6 changed=3 failed=0
web-02 : ok=6 changed=3 failed=0
web-03 : ok=6 changed=3 failed=0
web-04 : ok=5 changed=3 failed=1
steps.explanation: Batch 2 failed a health check on web-04, and Ansible stopped: web-05 to web-08 were never touched.
steps.why: This is the design working. The fleet is 3 hosts patched and healthy, 1 broken (and out of the load balancer), and 4 untouched. Without serial, all 8 would have rebooted into the same failure at once.

steps.prompt: Investigate web-04 only: check nginx's status with an ad-hoc command.
expected_commands: ansible web-04 -i inventory.ini -b -m command -a "systemctl status nginx"
ansible web-04 -i inventory.ini -b -m command -a 'systemctl status nginx'
ansible web-04 -i inventory.ini -b -m shell -a "systemctl status nginx"
steps.fake_output:
web-04 | FAILED | rc=3 >>
● nginx.service - A high performance web server
     Active: failed (Result: exit-code)
  nginx[912]: nginx: [emerg] unknown directive "ssl_reject_handshake" in /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/legacy:14
steps.explanation: web-04 has a leftover 'legacy' site config that the new nginx rejects.
steps.why: web-04 differs from its siblings: one extra config file. Rolling updates don't prevent drift, but they stop drift from turning into a fleet-wide outage. Fix the drift (remove the file through Ansible, not by hand), then rerun.

steps.prompt: After fixing it, resume from web-04 onwards: rerun patch.yml limited to web-04 through web-08 (the pattern web-0[4:8]).
steps.fake_output:
PLAY RECAP ***
web-04 : ok=6 changed=2 failed=0
web-05 : ok=6 changed=3 failed=0
web-06 : ok=6 changed=3 failed=0
web-07 : ok=6 changed=3 failed=0
web-08 : ok=6 changed=3 failed=0
steps.explanation: The rest of the fleet is patched, still in batches.
steps.why: Ansible also writes a retry file (patch.retry) listing failed hosts when retry_files_enabled is on, usable as '--limit @patch.retry'. Because playbooks are idempotent, simply rerunning the whole thing is also safe: already-patched hosts report ok and move on.
